deep_failures_counted_as_quick_better.note: the rule's own clause before amendment 2 ('deep returns no answer where quick answered')

excluding_asks_whose_quick_prose_was_wit.note: the grounding check withheld the light body's prose on 7 of 22 asks (L1, L5, L9, D1, D3, D4, D5), and 5 of the 7 deep wins are among them: part of deep's edge here is the light body failing its own grounding check on deepseek-v4.1-flash, not depth

calibration_of_the_judge.pre_registered_test: Fisher exact one-sided on the judged tier: p = 0.4, NOT better than chance. The judge called 3 of 16 heavy (D4, D3, D11); 2 of them were deep_better, and 5 of the 7 deep_better asks were judged light.
calibration_of_the_judge.exploratory_not_decisive: p_heavy as a continuous score ranks the deep_better asks well (AUC 0.865, permutation p 0.00625), and so does steps_implied_score (AUC 0.907): the judge's argmax tier throws away a signal its probabilities carry. But the candidate list's own diagnostic/descriptive label (written before the run, no model) does about as well (AUC 0.817; 6 of 8 diagnostic vs 1 of 8 descriptive deep_better), so the judge has not yet beaten a one-line rule, and a p_heavy threshold picked on these 16 would be fitted here and needs held-out asks.
calibration_of_the_judge.power: n = 16 with 3 called heavy: a one-sided Fisher p below 0.05 needed the judge to call heavy on at least 4 asks nearly all deep_better

verdict: CP-3 STAYS HELD, the rule's 'a_without_b'. (a) holds: deep beat quick on 7 of 16 valid asks (44 percent), 6 of 8 diagnostic and 1 of 8 descriptive, for about 1.8x the tokens; quick beat deep on 2 (L2, L10) and 7 tied. (b) fails: the judge's tier predicts those asks no better than chance (Fisher one-sided p = 0.4; it called 3 heavy, and 5 of the 7 asks where deep was worth it were called light). The next lever is the judge, not the router: its p_heavy and steps_implied carry the signal its argmax discards (exploratory AUC 0.865 / 0.907), but no better yet than a plain diagnostic-or-not rule. Every number is conditional: both arms ran on deepseek-v4.1-flash through the fallback (the Anthropic balance is spent), deep never answered 6 of 22 asks, and the light body's grounding check withheld 7 of its 22 answers.

After about 15 minutes of failing over on every call, the copy's API stopped failing over at all (11:20Z: Anthropic 400, no OpenRouter attempt) until it was restarted; cause not established (aughor/llm/provider.py, _complete_via_fallback / _fallback_provider).

On deepseek-v4.1-flash the light body's grounding check withheld its prose on 7 of 22 turns ('I could not ground this answer in the query result').
